Required to subscribe for free trial. To unlock the “free 3 day trial” you must subscribe to a monthly auto renewal of $6.99. These apps are hoping a significant portion of their free trial users will forget to unsubscribe. Just make the app 99¢ a month from day one with a 24hr unsubscribe trial period and I am good. At that point I know what I am signing up for and the cost is low enough to ignore. 
Not an issue for this app per-se but Apple should create an all you can eat subscription service for all $1.99 a month and less apps.

So fast!. Bug ID is so fast! I took a pic of this creepy-crawly and within seconds it told me it was a black widow spider. Scary! but good to know. The app even showed me what to do if I see one again. It's like having a bug expert in my pocket. I love how easy it is to use. Just snap a photo and you get all this cool info about the bug. My kids love playing bug detective with it too. We're learning so much about insects now. One thing though - sometimes it gets confused if the bug isn't fully in focus. But overall, this app is awesome.

The first one it said was “ant” I know that a freaking ant looks like, it was not an ant. Useless for my needs

This app is LIT!. Super easy to use and helps me ID bugs FAST. I can save my finds in collections perfect for my bio class and hiking adventures. Love how it tells me if bugs are harmless. Deets on insects make this app LIT!

Perfect tool for entomologists! 🐞. As an entomology student, Bug ID really makes it easier to complete my tasks! The identification is very accurate, and the descriptions are useful even for me. I also like the collections feature, it's very convenient to save insects from different places that I need to explore.

LIFE-SAVER❤️. You don’t even know how stressed I was before getting this app😫
 I live in an area with a rich insect life, which really freaks me out as a pet owner. I’m always scared my cat may be in danger because of an accidentally swallowed spider or god forbid any toxic bug. That’s why I needed an app that would help me identify bugs 100% accurately and tell me if they’re cat safe. 😊🤌
Thanks to Bug ID, I don’t have to spend hours on google trying to match the bug I saw in the kitchen with the photos on the internet. This app tells me all I need to know about the insects around me, which I’m 100% satisfied with🔝🔝🔝

Teaches how to coexist with insects. I recently moved to a house not far from the forest. Unfortunately, along with the fresh air and bird songs, my house also got filled with insects. I don’t feel good about killing them, so my friend advised me to download an app that identifies insects and even tells if they benefit people. I’ve lived for 30 years and didn’t know that insects can be good for people lol. I downloaded a few apps, and honestly, Bug ID is my favorite. The insect descriptions are really detailed, covering everything you might want to know. I especially like that the app indicates whether each insect is harmful to people, animals, plants, or other insects. For instance, I found a frightening and ugly (sorry) centipede, and it turned out it’s very useful for a house because it eats mosquitoes. Now, I look at it and comfort myself that it’s good, and it doesn’t look so bad anymore. So, the app is great! I recommend it to everyone who is looking for a way to coexist with insects!

Insect encyclopedia. My child needed to make a project about insects, which was quite challenging for me since I'm afraid of insects and know very little about them. Another mom from school suggested trying the Bug ID app, as it not only identifies insects but also provides detailed information about them. The biggest advantage of the app is its clear and user-friendly interface. I used it to identify a few insects in our yard with my son, and then he was able to finish the task on his own. The insect descriptions are incredibly thorough, resembling a real encyclopedia. They cover everything from appearance and distribution to their impact on other organisms. This app has been a true blessing for us!

Great for nature explorers!. I've been using Bug ID for some time now, and it's pretty great. The app is a breeze to use, making it a snap to identify any insect I find. It’s very convenient to store my discoveries in collections, which is perfect for my entomology studies and research. But even if you’re not that into bugs, I think it’ll come in handy for anyone who has a garden or just worried if any insect can be harmful or dangerous. So yeah, I recommend it for anyone interested in entomology like me or just curious about the creepy crawlies around them!
